-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in scrub habitats and where staggerbush occurs.

## Natural history notes

A host-specific gall-forming fungus characterized by the pinkish to whitish, swollen, distorted growths it produces on rusty staggerbush, Lyonia ferruginea. In Florida, it is associated with scrub and other habitats where rusty staggerbush occurs, including places such as central Florida scrub systems. Rather than forming a typical mushroom, it infects plant tissue and causes abnormal enlargement of leaves, flowers, or shoots, eventually producing a pale powdery or felt-like spore-bearing surface on the gall.
